scripts.//: The default bundle: the element and codejar, no highlighter — a docs site that already loads highlight.js should not ship a second copy.
The same element with highlight.js bundled in, for a page that has none. Same options as above, so the only difference between the two bundles is the entry file.

The options panel, opt-in and on top of either bundle above. It reaches the element through the custom element registry rather than through an import, so this bundle carries none of element.ts — a page loads one element bundle and this, and pays for the element once.

styles.//: Plain css in, plain css out — the point is a shipped dist/ that a consumer can link without a build of their own.
Optional syntax colors, kept separate so a site with its own theme is not overridden.

copy.//: The site loads no highlighter of its own, so it takes the bundle that brings one. No code-preview-hljs.css either — the docs theme colors the tokens, which is the case the separate stylesheet exists to allow.

The prose layout links css/prose.min.css. Prebuilt, so the site does not compile the theme's scss to use one page of it — and only the prose half of it, since the docs bundle is an alternative, not a layer.

options.//llms: The index and the corpus. `full` is the one that earns its place here: this is a one-page site, so the link map is a single line — the page's own prose is what an assistant answering questions about the element needs.
options.//sitemap: Also what turns the llms files on: poops 2.0.0 collects page entries only when searchIndex, sitemap, nav or feed is set, and llms is not in that list — with llms alone nothing is written. A sitemap is worth having on a published page regardless, so it is the cheap way to satisfy it.

site.title: code-preview
site.description: A code block that renders itself: live, editable HTML samples in an isolated iframe.
site.//jsonld: The prose layout emits the jsonld filter's block; this makes it TechArticle rather than the auto-detected WebPage, which is what a docs page is.

serve.//: No `base` — since 2.0 it defaults to the markup `out`, which is what it was set to.

//watch: dist is watched too: the copy sources above are build outputs, and without an event on them the copy into _site never re-runs — src edits would rebuild dist and reload a page still serving the previous bundle.
